newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends up on low demand for dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends up on low demand for dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed up on Thursday, as banks were reluctant to buy the dollar as the Central Bank seemed lukewarm towards the currency and because of the low level of imports, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.55 to the dollar, after opening at 58.75.
"Banks seemed uncomfortable buying dollars since the Central Bank pushed up the currency only by one cent," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by one local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.3605 and 59.5395.
Low commercial demand has also made banks a bit uncomefortable holding dollars, dealers said.
Overnight call money closed at its opening level of 9.75.
